checks.claim: The U.S. Department of Energy recommends setting a water heater's thermostat to 120 degrees Fahrenheit.
checks.why: Several plumbing and extension sources cite the Department of Energy's 120 F recommendation; heaters often ship at 140 F.

sources.title: University of Florida IFAS: water heating
Should you adjust your water heater temperature

checks.claim: A tank water heater's dip tube carries incoming cold water to the bottom of the tank so it does not mix with the hot water at the top.
checks.why: The dip tube sends cold inlet water to the tank bottom; a broken one lets cold water mix at the top and the tap runs lukewarm.

sources.title: What Is a Water Heater Dip Tube? (HomeServe)

checks.claim: A water heater's anode rod, usually magnesium or aluminum, corrodes instead of the steel tank.
checks.why: The rod is a more active metal than the steel, so it corrodes first; once it is gone, the tank rusts.
